newsitem.title: USA: Heir sells 9 million shares for $720 million.
newsitem.headline: Heir sells 9 million shares for $720 million.

text.p: John Dorrance III, the grandson of the founder of Campbell Soup Co., sold 9 million shares of Campbell stock worth $720 million Thursday in one of the largest single trades ever on the New York Stock Exchange.

Dorrance has been selling Campbell stock in recent weeks in an apparent bid to cash in on the strength of the shares. The company announced a major restructuring and stock buyback programme on Sept. 5 that has boosted the price of the shares.
The latest sale brings the total value of Campbell stock that Dorrance has sold since Sept. 23 to $1.3 billion.
Campbell said it was not involved in the trade, which crossed at $80 a share, off $3 from Wednesday's closing price, on the New York Stock Exchange at 12:32 p.m. EST.
The Camden, N.J.-based soup and food company later confirmed that the shares sold had been owned by Dorrance, the grandson of Campbell founder Dr. John Dorrance.

J.P. Morgan & Co. Inc. handled the trade and probably lined up the buyers, Wall Street sources said. Campbell said in its brief statement that the buyers included a "number of leading growth-oriented institutions."
Dorrance, an Irish citizen and avid racing fan who owns a number of horses, was not available for comment.
The trade, equal to almost 4 percent of Campbell's 247 million shares outstanding, was not part of the company's share buyback plan, a Campbell spokesman said.
The NYSE said the trade was the seventh biggest block trade in dollar terms ever on the exchange, and the largest in 3-1/2 years.

The Campbell spokesman said the company has not had any contact with Dorrance since he resigned from the board of directors last year. Two of Dorrance's siblings and two cousins remain on Campbell's 15-member board.

In filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission on Oct. 7 and Oct. 10, Dorrance said he had sold two blocks of Campbell stock -- one of 4.1 million shares and the second of 3.4 million shares -- since Sept. 23 at about $78 a share.

Those sales -- worth some $585 million before commissions -- had cut his holdings to about 15.9 million shares, or 6.4 percent of the company, the filings said. The first filing noted he would sell more shares as opportunities arose.
A lawyer mentioned in the SEC filings also was not available for comment.
Campbell stock fell $3 to close at $80 on the New York Stock Exchange where volume of 10.3 million shares made it the most active issue.
